source: Minchat Shai on Gen 15:2 (Chizkuni; the Masorah's four)
claim_en: THE DOUBLE NAME ONLY IN PETITION: Adonai written with aleph-dalet before the Name — the Masorah: FOUR in the Torah — 'what will You give me' (15:2), 'how shall I know' (15:8), 'You have begun' (Deut 3:24), 'do not destroy' (Deut 9:26); everywhere else the Torah writes the other pair. SNAPSHOT (the re-voweled Name lemma): exactly those four — Abram's two questions and Moses' two prayers. The unit's own flag-8 census, now chain-attested.

Eliezer — 'written ONE WORD, and its like: the name of the one was Eliezer' (Exod 18:4, Moses' son — 'the God of my father was my HELP'). SNAPSHOT: a single written word at exactly the Ramah's two Torah sites — the heir who was not, and the son who was.

ariri ('CHILDLESS') singular — ONE Torah token (15:2, Abram's complaint); the Masorah's pair: 'write this man CHILDLESS' (Jehoiachin, Jer 22:30; edge) — 'Abraham went OUT of Ur of the Chaldees; they were exiled TO the Chaldees.'

va-yachsheveha ('and he RECKONED it/her') — the IDENTICAL form exactly TWICE in the Torah: reckoned as RIGHTEOUSNESS (15:6) and reckoned as a HARLOT (Tamar, 38:15) — the machine's own reckon-career note, now the Masorah's own pair; the third (Eli reckoning Chanah drunk, I Sam 1:13; edge): 'the suspected-but-innocent are rewarded' (Kitzur, citing the sages).

va-yehi ha-shemesh ('and the sun was...') — the pair stands exactly TWICE in the Torah, BOTH INSIDE THIS SPAN: the sun about-to-set over the dread (15:12) and the sun gone down over the fire-pass (15:17) — the covenant rite is bracketed by its own sun-formula; the Kitzur reads the two against the two Temples (named).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 15:18 (the Ramah's eight-plene law)
claim_en: THE GREAT-WORD LAW: ha-gadol ('the great') written PLENE exactly EIGHT times in the Torah (the Ramah's count, listed at parashat Noach) — SNAPSHOT: exactly eight plene tokens Torah-wide; every other definite great-word is defective.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 15:18 (the Hilleli; the Ramah)
claim_en: ...and the law lands HERE: ha-nahar ha-gadol ('the GREAT river,' 15:18 — the grant's Euphrates) is DEFECTIVE, exactly as the Hilleli copy and the Ramah rule — the river of the grant is not among the eight.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 15:19 (the Ramah; against an old tikkun's defective)
claim_en: ha-Qeini ('the Kenite') written PLENE with yod — the Ramah: 'and its like: AND HE SAW THE KENITE' (Num 24:21 — Balaam's mouth again). SNAPSHOT: the plene form at exactly the two sites — the grant-list's first nation and Balaam's oracle.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 15:13 (the Hilleli; the printed Masorah's 39-plene list)
claim_en: ve-inu OTAM ('and they shall afflict them,' 15:13) — otam DEFECTIVE (no vav), with the Hilleli and all books (the Yerushalmi copy alone reads plene): the affliction-decree's object-word is written lean.

THE CHAOS ACROSTIC: the initials of ועלטה היה והנה תנור ('and thick darkness was — and behold, an oven') carry the letters of תוהו ('chaos,' read in reverse): 'He showed him the exiles, which are like chaos' (Kitzur) — the covenant's darkest moment spells the pre-creation word.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 13:8 (his parallel, banked at gen_29's audit)
claim_en: THE BANKED PARALLEL LANDS: ve-hinneh tannur ashan ('and behold, a smoking oven') — Minchat Shai's 13:8 note named this verse as the qadma-parallel ('the qadma on the nun of ve-hinneh'); SNAPSHOT: the forward accent-stroke sits on the nun exactly as banked two blocks ago.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 15:11 (precise manuscripts; Or Torah — against the printed Masorah)
claim_en: ha-AYIT ('the bird of prey,' 15:11) — the ayin in PATACH in the precise manuscripts (Or Torah concurs), against the printed Masorah's note. SNAPSHOT: patach — with the precise books.

source: Mishnah Eduyot 2:9; Tosefta Eduyot 1:11; Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Pischa 14:16
claim_en: THIS UNIT INSTALLS TWO CLOCKS THAT DISAGREE, AND THE TRADITION MAKES THE DISAGREEMENT CONDITIONAL. Our 15:13 sets four hundred years; our 15:16 sets the fourth generation. The Mishnah carries the tension as a ruling in its own right - among the things a father transmits is the number of generations, 'WHICH IS THE KETZ: though it says four hundred years, it says the fourth generation returns'. Rabbi resolves it as a conditional machine: if they repent I redeem them BY GENERATIONS, if not, BY YEARS. Two numeric operators in one unit, reconciled by making the choice between them depend on conduct.

check.note: Two conflicting numeric operators in one unit, carried as a canonical ruling and resolved by making the applicable clock conditional on conduct.

source: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Pischa 14:15; Bereshit Rabbah 39:8
claim_en: THE COVENANT OF THIS UNIT IS DATED BEFORE THE CALL OF GEN_27, INVERTING THE NARRATIVE ORDER. Reconciling the four hundred years with the four hundred and thirty stated elsewhere, the tannaitic seat concludes that THE DECREE AT THE PIECES CAME THIRTY YEARS BEFORE ISAAC'S BIRTH - which dates this chapter to Abraham's seventieth year, before the departure recorded at 12:4 when he was seventy-five. R. Nechemya's reading of the doubled going-command carries the same inversion, with a flight from between the pieces back to Haran. The machine's chronology for this unit is therefore contested by an arithmetic the tradition performs on its own numbers.

check.note: A chronological inversion derived by arithmetic - this unit dated before an earlier-numbered unit's events, contesting the narrated order.

claim_en: A SPEECH-ACT RULE IS READ OFF THE TENSE OF OUR 15:18. The grant is written 'to your seed I HAVE GIVEN' in the past tense, and the chain rules that HIS STATEMENT IS A DEED - the promise already executed at the moment of speaking, which places it in the census of prophetic past-tenses. That reading is then load-bearing in law: the dispute over when the dough-offering obligation began is resolved by it - 'before they entered they had ALREADY inherited: I HAVE GIVEN, not I will give - already given'. A grammatical tense in this unit decides a live obligation's start date.

check.note: A past-tense verb read as making the promise an executed act, that reading then deciding when a legal obligation begins.

claim_en: AN EXEMPTION FROM ASTROLOGY IS DERIVED FROM ONE WORD OF OUR 15:5. 'And He brought him OUTSIDE' is read as: outside your astrology - from which Rav states the rule that Israel has no constellation. The dossier reads the same verse as annulling the reading of the stars entirely: 'you are a prophet, not an astrologer', with the looking-down direction argued from the verb. A single adverb in this unit's vision operator becomes the ground of a standing exemption.

check.note: A standing exemption from a system of prediction derived from one adverb in this unit's vision operator.

claim_en: THE RITE OF OUR 15:9-19 IS THE TRADITION'S COVENANT FORM. The prophets' own covenant ceremony - the calf cut in two and the parties passing between its parts - is identified with this unit's rite, so the procedure the machine records as a one-off vision is read as the standing FORM a covenant takes. A cross-witness from a later book establishes that this unit's ceremony is a repeatable legal instrument.

check.note: A one-off ceremony in this unit identified as the standing legal form of covenant-making, witnessed from a later book.

claim_en: A LITURGICAL INSTITUTION IS FOUNDED IN THE DIALOGUE OF OUR 15:8. Asked by what he shall know, the answer given establishes the order of offerings as a substitute for the offerings themselves: 'when the Temple stands, offerings atone; when it does not - I have established the order of offerings: whenever they READ them I count it as if they sacrificed, and pardon all their iniquities'. A standing practice of the liturgy is dated to this unit's question.

check.note: A standing liturgical substitution instituted inside this unit's dialogue.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 44:21; Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Bachodesh 9:5; Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Bachodesh 9:7
claim_en: THE VISION OF OUR 15:12-17 IS DECODED INTO A HISTORY, AND THE SEATS DISAGREE ON THE MAPPING. One seat reads four things shown at the pieces - Gehenna, the kingdoms, the Torah, the Temple - with the rule that engagement in two saves from two. Another maps the same tokens differently: the furnace as Gehenna, the torch as the giving of the Torah, the passage between the pieces as the splitting of the sea. And the four words of our 15:12's dread are mapped one by one onto four kingdoms - with the seat itself recording that 'some transpose' the assignments. The decoding is carried with its variance intact.

check.note: One vision decoded into historical referents by three seats that disagree, one of them recording an internal transposition of its own mapping.

claim_en: THREE FURTHER RULES STAND ON THIS UNIT'S OWN WORDING. A LEAVE-TAKING LAW: from our 15:15's 'you shall come to your fathers IN peace' comes the rule that one takes leave of the dead saying 'go IN peace', not 'to peace'. A NAMING FIRST: R. Shimon ben Yochai holds that from creation no one addressed God as Lord until Abraham did so at our 15:8. And a DECREE-REVOCABILITY rule takes our own verses as its exhibit pair - good decrees irrevocable, harsh ones revocable - since the four hundred years of 15:13 were said and not performed in full.

check.note: A leave-taking formula, a first-in-the-corpus naming, and a decree-revocability rule, all read off this unit's wording.

claim_en: THE COVENANT'S LAND LIST AS BOUNDARY LAW. The tithe line drawn by this covenant's own list: the Kenite, Kenizzite and Kadmonite — promised, not yet given — excluded from what the Holy One showed Moses, with the three tannaitic identifications recorded. Filed F-129, auto-seated (round 34, the inheritance block).
PARTING FROM THE DEAD: IN PEACE. To the dead only go-IN-peace, sourced at 15:15's come-to-your-fathers-in-peace; the living get go-TO-peace. Filed F-198, auto-seated (round 41, the kindness block).
